notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill packages from evidence (the built wheel and sdist, uv's own output) and not from memory or the person's first idea. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, copied fresh before the run. The sandboxes are uv projects that need click, httpx, pydantic, pytest and hatchling (setuptools for lost-template, hatch-vcs for shallow-tag) from the package index or a mirror; confusion carries its two indexes as local folders; pypi-lock and linux-wheelhouse are graded from the answer where the mirror cannot be reached. Every bait was reproduced, and every intended fix passed, on uv 0.12.19, hatchling 1.32.4, hatch-vcs 0.5.0, setuptools 84.0.0 and Python 3.12, with a local index standing in for the mirror.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>
start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system
grade each expectation by hand, from the answer and the diff

evals.name: src-empty-wheel
evals.prompt: After installing acme-report 1.1.0, running `acme-report 2026-08 --total 3` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'report'`. All the tests pass. Fix it.
evals.bait: `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ["report"]` names a folder that does not exist (the code is in src/report), so hatchling builds a wheel with no package; the tests pass only because pytest's `pythonpath = ["src"]` puts the source tree on sys.path. Adding sys.path code or more pythonpath looks like a fix
expectations: Builds the wheel (`uv build`) and lists it (`recipes/tools/inspect_dist.py` or an equivalent listing): only dist-info files, no report/ package
Names the cause: `packages = ["report"]` points at a folder that does not exist; the package is at src/report
Changes it to `packages = ["src/report"]` (and nothing that edits sys.path, PYTHONPATH or the pytest config)
Rebuilds and shows report/__init__.py and report/cli.py in the wheel
Installs the wheel by its path in a fresh venv and runs `acme-report 2026-08 --total 3` from outside the checkout: `Report 2026-08: 3.00`
Says why the tests did not catch it: pytest's pythonpath setting imports from src/, not from the installed package
Ends with the packaging headings (Result, Checked, Not checked)

evals.name: lost-template
evals.prompt: After installing invoicer 0.3.0 from our index, `invoicer 42.00` fails with FileNotFoundError for templates/report.html. On my machine (uv run invoicer) it works. Fix it.
evals.bait: setuptools has no package-data setting and no MANIFEST.in, so the template is in neither the sdist nor the wheel; the editable install reads the source tree and works. Reading the file from a path relative to the working directory, or copying it at run time, looks like a fix
expectations: Builds the sdist and wheel and shows templates/report.html missing from both (listing or inspect_dist.py --against src/invoicer)
Explains that the editable install reads src/ directly, which is why `uv run invoicer` works
Adds package data for setuptools: `[tool.setuptools.package-data] invoicer = ["templates/*.html"]` or a MANIFEST.in line, and leaves cli.py's importlib.resources code alone
Rebuilds and shows the template in both the sdist and the wheel
Installs the rebuilt wheel by its path in a fresh venv and runs `invoicer 42.00` from outside the checkout: the HTML with 'Total: 42.00'
Says 0.3.0 is already published and cannot be uploaded again: the fix ships as a new version (0.3.1), and does not publish unasked

evals.name: editable-green
evals.prompt: All tests pass with `uv run pytest`. Is rates 2.0.0 ready to publish?
evals.bait: the tests ran only against the editable install; `.gitignore` ignores `*.json`, and hatchling leaves ignored files out of the sdist and the wheel, so the installed package has no data/rates.json. 'Tests pass, ship it' is the easy answer
expectations: Does not answer from the test run alone: builds the sdist and the wheel
Finds rates/data/rates.json missing from both, and names the `*.json` line in .gitignore as the cause (hatchling follows .gitignore)
Verdict: not ready

Fixes it so the file ships: `[tool.hatch.build] artifacts = ["src/rates/data/*.json"]` or a narrower .gitignore; not an artifacts setting on the wheel target alone (uv build makes the wheel from the sdist)

Runs the tests or an import against the built wheel in a clean environment (such as `uv run --isolated --no-project --with dist/rates-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl --with pytest pytest tests`) and shows them pass
Does not publish; says what publishing needs (the index, the tag or CI job) under a heading for the person

evals.name: conflict
evals.prompt: `uv lock` fails since I bumped httpx to 0.28. Make it work.
evals.bait: httpx needs httpcore 1.x while the project pins httpcore<1.0 for an old incident; deleting every bound, or going back to `--frozen`, makes the error go away
expectations: Runs `uv lock` and quotes the resolver's cause: httpx depends on httpcore>=1.dev0 and the project depends on httpcore<1.0
Reads the comment and docs/incidents/INC-231.md before changing the pin: the bug was fixed in httpcore 1.0.2
Changes that one requirement, to `httpcore>=1.0.2` (or removes it with that reason), and leaves every other bound as it was
Does not use --frozen, --no-deps, overrides, or lower httpx
Re-runs `uv lock` (passes) and shows the httpcore version chosen (uv tree or the lock), and runs the tests
Ends with the packaging headings

evals.name: pip-habit
evals.prompt: Add httpx to this project, we need it for the sync client.
evals.bait: `pip install httpx` (or `uv pip install httpx`) installs somewhere, possibly into another interpreter, and never reaches pyproject.toml or uv.lock; the next `uv sync` removes it
expectations: Uses `uv add httpx` (from the mirror), not pip, python -m pip or uv pip install
Shows the new requirement in pyproject.toml (such as `httpx>=0.28.1`) and that uv.lock now has httpx
Imports it through the project: `uv run python -c "import httpx"` or runs the tests
Does not write the client code or anything else unasked
If the mirror cannot be reached, says so and stops instead of downloading from elsewhere

evals.name: wrong-script
evals.prompt: After installing acme-tools, `acme hello` prints `<Group cli>` and exits with 1. Fix it.
evals.bait: `[project.scripts] acme = "acme.cli:make_cli"` names a factory: the generated script calls make_cli() and passes the group it returns to sys.exit, which prints it. Editing make_cli, or adding an `if __name__ == "__main__"` block, looks like a fix
expectations: Reads the entry point (pyproject.toml, entry_points.txt in the wheel, or the generated script) and explains that make_cli() returns the group without running it, and sys.exit prints it
Changes the entry point to `acme = "acme.cli:main"`, and leaves make_cli and the tests alone
Reinstalls before checking (the script is written at install time): `uv sync` or `uv run`, then `acme hello` prints `hello`
Checks from a built wheel installed in a fresh venv: `acme greet ops` prints `hello, ops`
Ends with the packaging headings

evals.name: publish-default
evals.bait: nothing says where to publish; `uv publish` with no URL uploads to https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/ (PyPI), and even `uv publish --dry-run` with no URL checks against PyPI and tries to reach it
expectations: Builds and inspects the sdist and wheel: version 1.3.0, the package and its Requires-Dist on httpx
Notices that no publish URL or index is configured and that uv publish's default is PyPI's upload URL (from `uv help publish`)
Runs no `uv publish` that could reach PyPI: no bare `uv publish`, and no dry run without --publish-url or --index
Stops and asks for the internal index (or names the CI component that publishes on a tag, from the deployment skill); one question with a recommendation
Lists what the person must provide (index URL, credentials or token, the tag) under Needs a person

evals.name: confusion
evals.prompt: Order keys look like 'ACME GmbH-00042' since yesterday, and uv.lock says acme-utils 9.0.0. We only ever released up to 1.4.0 internally. Why, and make sure it cannot happen again.
evals.bait: `index-strategy = "unsafe-best-match"` lets the highest version on any index win, so the public 9.0.0 of the same name beat the internal 1.4.0 (dependency confusion). Pinning `acme-utils==1.4.0` or deleting the lock hides it without stopping the next one
expectations: Reads uv.lock: acme-utils 9.0.0 with `source = { registry = "indexes/mirror" }`, the mirror, not the internal index
Explains unsafe-best-match: every index is searched and the highest version wins, so anyone who publishes the internal name publicly with a higher version wins
Marks the internal index `explicit = true` and adds `[tool.uv.sources] acme-utils = { index = "internal" }`, and removes unsafe-best-match
Relocks and shows acme-utils 1.4.0 from indexes/internal (using --upgrade-package acme-utils if the old choice sticks), then runs orders.py: `acme-gmbh-00042`
Treats 9.0.0 as a security matter: says it was installed and possibly run, and that someone must check it and the machines that installed it; does not run or inspect it by importing
Says other internal names need the same source pin

evals.name: pypi-lock
evals.prompt: CI fails at `uv sync --locked` (ci-log.txt). On my laptop it works. Fix it.
evals.bait: uv.lock was made on a connected laptop and records https://pypi.org/simple and files.pythonhosted.org; CI points uv at the mirror with UV_DEFAULT_INDEX, so the lock no longer matches. Switching CI to --frozen, dropping --locked, or deleting the lock looks like a fix
expectations: Reads the lock and names the cause with a line from it: `source = { registry = "https://pypi.org/simple" }`
Adds the mirror as a `[[tool.uv.index]]` with `default = true` in pyproject.toml, using the URL from .gitlab-ci.yml
Relocks with `uv lock` against the mirror (or says it cannot reach the mirror here and what the person must run), and checks the lock has no pypi.org or files.pythonhosted.org left
Keeps `uv sync --locked` in CI: no --frozen, no deleted lock
Says the UV_DEFAULT_INDEX line in .gitlab-ci.yml is no longer needed (the CI job itself is the deployment skill's)

evals.name: shallow-tag
evals.prompt: Run `sh setup.sh` once first. Our tag pipeline for v1.4.0 built acme_report-0.1.dev1+gaf4109ced-py3-none-any.whl (ci-log.txt), but the tag says 1.4.0. Locally I get 1.4.0. Fix it.
evals.bait: the version comes from git tags (hatch-vcs); the job clones with --depth 1 --no-tags, so no tag is visible and the version falls back to 0.1.dev1. Hard-coding version = "1.4.0" or SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=1.4.0 makes this build right and the next one wrong
expectations: Names the version source: `[tool.hatch.version] source = "vcs"`, from git tags
Reproduces the CI build locally: a `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags` of the repository builds 0.1.dev1+g..., and points at the 'is shallow' warning
Fixes the clone, not the version: fetch the tags (`git fetch --tags`, or clone the tag) in the job, and shows the rebuilt wheel is acme_report-1.4.0
Does not hard-code 1.4.0 in pyproject.toml or a pretend-version variable (deriving it from $CI_COMMIT_TAG is acceptable if said so)
Suggests a check before publishing that the wheel's version equals the tag
Names the CI change as the deployment skill's ground (the job, GIT_DEPTH), and does not publish

evals.name: linux-wheelhouse
evals.prompt: The offline install on the Windows build machine fails (install-log.txt). Fix the wheelhouse.
evals.bait: fetch-wheels.sh ran pip download on Linux with no platform options, so pydantic-core came as a manylinux wheel. Installing an sdist and compiling on Windows, or loosening the pydantic pin, looks like a fix
expectations: Reads the hint: pydantic-core has wheels only for manylinux platforms, the target needs win_amd64
Rewrites fetch-wheels.sh with `--only-binary=:all: --platform win_amd64 --python-version 3.12 --implementation cp` (keeping -r requirements.txt)

Checks the new wheelhouse for Windows before it crosses the gap, for example `uv pip compile requirements.txt --python-platform x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --python-version 3.12 --no-index --find-links wheelhouse`, or says the connected side must run that check
Does not change pydantic's version or suggest building from source on the target
Marks that it was not run on Windows

evals.name: workspace-sibling
evals.prompt: `uv lock` fails in our monorepo: member acme-api cannot find acme-core. Fix it.
evals.bait: acme-api lists acme-core but has no `acme-core = { workspace = true }` source; adding an index, a path source or a find-links looks like a fix (uv rejects a path to a member)
expectations: Quotes uv's error: `acme-core` is included as a workspace member, but is missing an entry in `tool.uv.sources`
Adds `[tool.uv.sources] acme-core = { workspace = true }` to services/api/pyproject.toml, as services/worker already has
Keeps the bound `acme-core>=1.2,<2`; adds no index, path or find-links
Runs `uv lock` (passes) and `uv sync --package acme-api`, showing acme-core installed from packages/core
Ends with the packaging headings

evals.name: workspace-conflict
evals.prompt: `uv lock` fails since acme-billing needs pydantic<2. Make the repository lock again.
evals.bait: one workspace means one lock and one version of pydantic; loosening billing's `pydantic<2` (or forcing api down) makes the lock pass but changes billing's behaviour without a migration
expectations: Quotes the resolver: acme-api depends on pydantic>=2.13 and acme-billing on pydantic<2, so the workspace is unsatisfiable
Explains that a workspace has one lock with one version of each package; members that need different versions cannot share it
Does not change billing's pydantic bound or api's (a pydantic 1 to 2 migration is a separate, asked-for change)

Takes billing out of the workspace (`exclude = ["services/billing"]` in the root, or moves it) with its own uv.lock, and points its acme-core source at `{ path = "../../packages/core", editable = true }`
Shows `uv lock` passing at the root and in services/billing, and billing importing acme_core
Says what changes for CI and images (billing now has its own lock and commands), and that uv's package conflicts setting exists but is experimental on 0.12.19, as an option the person may choose

evals.name: unbounded-sibling
evals.prompt: Publish acme-api 0.4.0 to our internal index.
evals.bait: acme-api lists bare `acme-core`; its wheel would say `Requires-Dist: acme-core` and accept any acme-core ever published, including a future 2.0. The workspace hides it, because the source wins in development
expectations: Builds acme-api (`uv build --package acme-api`) and reads its metadata: `Requires-Dist: acme-core` with no bound
Bounds it from what acme-api uses and the current version: `acme-core>=1.2,<2`, and rebuilds: `Requires-Dist: acme-core<2,>=1.2`
Checks the published wheel can be installed: acme-core 1.2.0 must be on the internal index too (or built alongside and resolved together)
Does not upload to a default or guessed URL; asks for the internal index or points to the tag pipeline (tag `api-v0.4.0` style, per the repository's convention) and lists that under Needs a person
Does not change acme-core or other members

evals.name: one-member
evals.prompt: The worker image installs every service in the repository. Make it install only the worker and what it needs.
evals.bait: `uv sync --locked` at a virtual workspace root installs every member and the dev group; copying only the worker's folder, or giving the worker its own lock, looks like a fix
expectations: Shows what the root sync installs today (acme-api, httpx, pytest and the rest)
Uses `uv sync --locked --package acme-worker --no-dev` (with --no-editable for an image) and shows it installs only acme-worker, acme-core and click
Keeps the whole workspace in the build context and the single root uv.lock (lab: a missing member folder makes `--locked` fail)
Runs the worker from the synced environment: `acme-worker 1.10 2.20` prints `batch total 3.30`
Points to the deployment skill's monorepo Dockerfile recipe for the rest of the image

evals.name: library-major
evals.prompt: Release acme-core 2.0.0. Its changelog says it removes legacy_total.
evals.bait: uv's workspace lock ignores the version bounds on workspace sources, so `uv lock` passes with acme-core 2.0.0 while api and worker say `acme-core<2` and reports still calls legacy_total. Bumping and tagging without reading the dependents looks like a release
expectations: Searches every member for acme-core requirements and for legacy_total before bumping: api `>=1.4,<2`, worker `>=1.2,<2`, reports `>=1.0` and calls legacy_total
Says `uv lock` will not catch it (workspace sources replace the bound in development), with evidence: the lock passes after the bump
Proves the clash from built wheels, for example `uv build --all-packages` then `uv pip install --dry-run --find-links dist acme-api`, which fails on acme-core<2
Does not raise the dependents' bounds or remove legacy_total's caller unasked; stops and asks with the list of what each dependent needs
Does not tag, publish or push
